subproblem.title: Cylinders over H^m-null sets are H^{m+1}-null
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and write π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) ∈ ℝ^P for y = (y_0, …, y_P) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))). Let H^k := μHE[k] be Mathlib's normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure. If N ⊆ ℝ^P satisfies H^m(N) = 0, then the cylinder {y ∈ ℝ^{P+1} : π(y) ∈ N} = ℝ × N satisfies H^{m+1}({y : π(y) ∈ N}) = 0. (This is verbatim Part (a), the first conjunct, of the parent theorem.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (N : Set (Eucl P)), (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) N = 0 → (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1))) {y | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ N} = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source and scope. This is Part (a) of the parent proof of iwl_cr_hausdorff_product_formula (node root.integrality_weak_limits-a1.cycle_reduction-a1.hausdorff_product-a1, Steps 1–4), an elementary covering argument. The statement is verbatim the first conjunct of the parent's frozen type. The constants are slightly coarser than the parent's, which changes nothing in the argument and avoids square roots and real exponents:
- box diameters are bounded by 2·d_i instead of √2·d_i;
- each strip is cut into k_i := ⌊1/d_i⌋ + 1 boxes instead of ⌈1/d_i⌉.
No DAG declaration is used.

Conventions.
(C1) Coordinates. E := Eucl P and E′ := Eucl (P+1). For y ∈ E′ put y_0 := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y) 0 and π(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y)). Splitting off the 0-th coordinate (EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, Fin.sum_univ_succ) gives
  dist(y, y′)² = (y_0 − y′_0)² + dist(π y, π y′)².
(C2) Normalization. μH[d] is Mathlib's d-dimensional Hausdorff measure and ediam is the extended diameter (Metric.ediam).
- By Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, μHE[k] S = c_k · μH[k] S, where c_k := addHaarScalarFactor (volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) μH[k] ∈ ℝ≥0.
- c_k ≠ 0 by Measure.addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero.
- Hence μHE[k] S = 0 iff μH[k] S = 0. Here μH[k] means μH[(k : ℝ)].
(C3) N̂ := {y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ N}.

1. (Case m = 0.) μHE[0] = μH[0] (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), and μH[0]{x} = 1 for every point x (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). If some x ∈ N, monotonicity would give 1 ≤ μH[0](N) = μHE[0](N) = 0. Hence N = ∅, so N̂ = ∅ and μHE[1](N̂) = 0.

2. (Case m ≥ 1: reductions.) By (C2), μH[m](N) = 0, and it suffices to show μH[m+1](N̂) = 0.
- Strips. For a ∈ ℤ let S_a := {y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ N, a ≤ y_0 ≤ a + 1}. Every y ∈ N̂ lies in S_{⌊y_0⌋}, so N̂ ⊆ ⋃_{a∈ℤ} S_a. By countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null) it suffices to fix a ∈ ℤ and show μH[m+1](S_a) = 0.
- Unfolding the measure. By Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply,
  μH[m+1](S_a) = ⨆_{r>0} ⨅ { Σ_n ⨆_{t_n ≠ ∅} ediam(t_n)^{m+1} : t : ℕ → Set E′, S_a ⊆ ⋃_n t_n, ∀ n, ediam(t_n) ≤ r }.
- Fix r ∈ (0, ∞]. By ENNReal.le_of_forall_pos_le_add it suffices to show that the infimum belonging to r is ≤ η for every real η > 0. Since ⨆_{t_n≠∅} ediam(t_n)^{m+1} ≤ ediam(t_n)^{m+1}, it suffices to produce:
  (★) sets t_n (n ∈ ℕ) with S_a ⊆ ⋃_n t_n, ediam(t_n) ≤ r for all n, and Σ_n ediam(t_n)^{m+1} ≤ η.
- Fix η > 0.

3. (Parameters.) Choose δ ∈ (0, 1/2] with ENNReal.ofReal δ ≤ r: δ := 1/2 if r = ∞, and δ := min(1/2, r/2) otherwise. Put ε := min((δ/2)^m/2, η/2^{m+3}). Then ε > 0, ε < (δ/2)^m and 2^{m+3}·ε ≤ η.

4. (Covering N.) Consider the infimum in hausdorffMeasure_apply for μH[m](N) at the radius ENNReal.ofReal(δ/2) > 0.
- It is ≤ the supremum μH[m](N) = 0 (iSup₂_eq_bot), hence < ofReal ε.
- Unfolding the three infima (iInf_lt_iff) gives C : ℕ → Set E with N ⊆ ⋃_i C_i, ediam(C_i) ≤ ofReal(δ/2) for all i, and Σ_i ⨆_{C_i ≠ ∅} ediam(C_i)^m < ofReal ε.
- As m ≥ 1, ediam(∅)^m = 0, so the factor ⨆_{C_i≠∅} can be dropped (iSup_pos, iSup_neg, ENNReal.rpow_natCast): Σ_i ediam(C_i)^m < ofReal ε.
- Each ediam(C_i) is finite. Put D_i := (ediam C_i).toReal. Then ediam C_i = ofReal D_i and 0 ≤ D_i ≤ δ/2. Also dist(x, x′) ≤ D_i for x, x′ ∈ C_i (edist_le_ediam_of_mem).

5. (Inflated sizes.)
- Put λ_i := (ε/2/2^i)/(δ/2)^m. Then 0 < λ_i ≤ 1, because ε/2/2^i ≤ ε < (δ/2)^m.
- Put ρ_i := (δ/2)·λ_i. Then 0 < ρ_i ≤ δ/2, and ρ_i^m = (δ/2)^m·λ_i^m ≤ (δ/2)^m·λ_i = ε/2/2^i, since λ_i^m ≤ λ_i for 0 ≤ λ_i ≤ 1 and m ≥ 1.
- Put d_i := max(D_i, ρ_i). Then 0 < d_i ≤ δ/2 ≤ 1/4 and D_i ≤ d_i. Also d_i^m ≤ D_i^m + ε/2/2^i (consider which term is the maximum).

6. (Boxes.) Let k_i := ⌊1/d_i⌋ + 1 ∈ ℕ (Nat.floor). Since ⌊1/d_i⌋ ≤ 1/d_i and 1 ≤ 1/d_i, we have k_i ≤ 2/d_i. For j ∈ ℕ put
  Q_{i,j} := {y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ C_i, a + j·d_i ≤ y_0 ≤ a + (j+1)·d_i}.
(i) Diameter. For y, y′ ∈ Q_{i,j}, |y_0 − y′_0| ≤ d_i and dist(π y, π y′) ≤ D_i ≤ d_i. By (C1), dist(y, y′)² ≤ 2d_i² ≤ (2d_i)², i.e. dist(y, y′) ≤ 2d_i. Hence ediam Q_{i,j} ≤ ofReal(2d_i) ≤ ofReal δ ≤ r (Metric.ediam_le_of_forall_dist_le).
(ii) Cover. Let y ∈ S_a and choose i with π(y) ∈ C_i. Put u := (y_0 − a)/d_i ∈ [0, 1/d_i] and j := ⌊u⌋. Then j ≤ ⌊1/d_i⌋ < k_i (Nat.floor_le_floor) and j ≤ u < j + 1. Hence a + j·d_i ≤ y_0 < a + (j+1)·d_i, and y ∈ Q_{i,j}.

7. (The countable family.) For n ∈ ℕ with (i, j) := Nat.unpair n, let t_n := Q_{i,j} if j < k_i, and t_n := ∅ otherwise. Thus t(Nat.pair i j) = Q_{i,j} whenever j < k_i (Nat.unpair_pair). By 6(ii), S_a ⊆ ⋃_n t_n. By 6(i) and ediam ∅ = 0, ediam t_n ≤ r for all n.

8. (The sum.) Using Nat.pairEquiv (Equiv.tsum_eq) and ENNReal.tsum_prod,
  Σ_n ediam(t_n)^{m+1} = Σ_i Σ_j ediam(t(Nat.pair i j))^{m+1}.
- Fix i. Only the j < k_i contribute (tsum_eq_sum over Finset.range k_i), each at most ofReal(2d_i)^{m+1}. Using step 5 and ediam(C_i)^m = ofReal(D_i^m), the inner sum is
  ≤ ofReal(k_i·(2d_i)^{m+1}) ≤ ofReal((2/d_i)·2^{m+1}·d_i^{m+1}) = ofReal(2^{m+2}·d_i^m) ≤ ofReal(2^{m+2})·(ediam(C_i)^m + ofReal(ε/2/2^i)).
- Sum over i (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left, ENNReal.tsum_add). We have Σ_i ediam(C_i)^m < ofReal ε (step 4) and Σ_i ofReal(ε/2/2^i) = ofReal ε (tsum_geometric_two', ENNReal.ofReal_tsum_of_nonneg). Hence
  Σ_n ediam(t_n)^{m+1} ≤ ofReal(2^{m+2})·(ofReal ε + ofReal ε) = ofReal(2^{m+3}·ε) ≤ ofReal η = η.
This proves (★).

9. (Conclusion.) By (★) and step 2, μH[m+1](S_a) = 0 for every a ∈ ℤ. Hence μH[m+1](N̂) = 0, and μHE[m+1](N̂) = c_{m+1}·0 = 0 by (C2). With step 1, the statement holds for all m. ∎

theorem Submission.iwl_cr_hp_cylinder_null : ∀ (P m : ℕ) (N : Set (Eucl P)), (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) N = 0 → (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1))) {y | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ N} = 0 := by
  intro P m N hN
  have hE : ∀ (k : ℕ) {X : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [InnerProductSpace ℝ X]
      [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (S : Set X), (μHE[k] : Measure X) S =
        (Measure.addHaarScalarFactor (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))) μH[k] : ℝ≥0∞) *
          μH[k] S := by
    intro k X _ _ _ _ S
    rw [Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, Measure.smul_apply, ENNReal.smul_def, smul_eq_mul]
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos m with rfl | hm
  · -- `m = 0`: a `μH[0]`-null set is empty
    have hNe : N = ∅ := by
      by_contra hne
      obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mpr hne
      have h1 : μH[0] ({x} : Set (Eucl P)) ≤ μH[0] N := measure_mono (singleton_subset_iff.mpr hx)
      rw [Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton] at h1
      rw [Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero] at hN
      rw [hN] at h1
      exact absurd h1 (by simp)
    subst hNe
    simp
  · have hcm : (Measure.addHaarScalarFactor (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)))
        μH[m] : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0 := by
      exact_mod_cast Measure.addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero m
    have hNm : μH[(m : ℝ)] N = 0 := by
      rw [hE m N] at hN
      exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hN).resolve_left hcm
    rw [hE (m + 1)]
    suffices h : μH[((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)] {y : Eucl (P + 1) | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm
        (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ N} = 0 by rw [h, mul_zero]
    have hsub : {y : Eucl (P + 1) | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm
        (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ N} ⊆ ⋃ a : ℤ, {y : Eucl (P + 1) |
          (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ N ∧
          (a : ℝ) ≤ EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y 0 ∧
          EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y 0 ≤ a + 1} := by
      intro y hy
      exact mem_iUnion.2 ⟨⌊EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y 0⌋, hy, Int.floor_le _,
        (Int.lt_floor_add_one _).le⟩
    have hstrip : ∀ a : ℤ, μH[((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)] {y : Eucl (P + 1) |
        (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ N ∧
        (a : ℝ) ≤ EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y 0 ∧
        EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y 0 ≤ a + 1} = 0 := by
      intro a
      set π : Eucl (P + 1) → Eucl P := fun y =>
        (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y))
        with hπdef
      set y0 : Eucl (P + 1) → ℝ := fun y => EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y 0 with hy0def
      have hdist : ∀ y y' : Eucl (P + 1),
          dist y y' ^ 2 = (y0 y - y0 y') ^ 2 + dist (π y) (π y') ^ 2 := by
        intro y y'
        rw [EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity),
          Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity), Fin.sum_univ_succ]
        simp [hπdef, hy0def, Fin.tail, Real.dist_eq, sq_abs]
      have hm0 : (0 : ℝ) < m := by exact_mod_cast hm
      apply le_antisymm _ zero_le
      rw [Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply]
      refine iSup₂_le fun r hr => ?_
      refine ENNReal.le_of_forall_pos_le_add fun η hη _ => ?_
      rw [zero_add]
      -- the radius
      obtain ⟨δ, hδ0, hδ1, hδr⟩ : ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ δ ≤ 1 / 2 ∧ ENNReal.ofReal δ ≤ r := by
        rcases eq_or_ne r ⊤ with rfl | hrt
        · exact ⟨1 / 2, by norm_num, le_rfl, le_top⟩
        · have hr' : 0 < r.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hr.ne' hrt
          refine ⟨min (1 / 2) (r.toReal / 2), by positivity, min_le_left _ _, ?_⟩
          calc ENNReal.ofReal (min (1 / 2) (r.toReal / 2)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal r.toReal :=
                ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal ((min_le_right _ _).trans (by linarith))
            _ = r := ENNReal.ofReal_toReal hrt
      -- the smallness parameter
      have hη0 : (0 : ℝ) < η := hη
      set ε : ℝ := min ((δ / 2) ^ m / 2) (η / 2 ^ (m + 3)) with hεdef
      have hε0 : 0 < ε := by positivity
      have hεδ : ε < (δ / 2) ^ m := by
        have : 0 < (δ / 2) ^ m := by positivity
        exact (min_le_left _ _).trans_lt (by linarith)
      have hεη : 2 ^ (m + 3) * ε ≤ η := by
        have h := min_le_right ((δ / 2) ^ m / 2) (η / 2 ^ (m + 3))
        rw [← hεdef] at h
        have h2 : (0 : ℝ) < 2 ^ (m + 3) := by positivity
        calc 2 ^ (m + 3) * ε ≤ 2 ^ (m + 3) * (η / 2 ^ (m + 3)) := by gcongr
          _ = η := by field_simp
      -- a cover of `N`

      rw [Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply] at hNa
      have hδ2 : (0 : ℝ≥0∞) < ENNReal.ofReal (δ / 2) := ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr (by positivity)
      have hF := (iSup₂_eq_bot.mp hNa) (ENNReal.ofReal (δ / 2)) hδ2
      have hlt : (⨅ (t : ℕ → Set (Eucl P)) (_ : N ⊆ ⋃ n, t n)
          (_ : ∀ n, ediam (t n) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (δ / 2)),
            ∑' n, ⨆ _ : (t n).Nonempty, ediam (t n) ^ (m : ℝ)) < ENNReal.ofReal ε := by
        rw [hF]; exact ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr hε0
      obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := iInf_lt_iff.mp hlt
      obtain ⟨hCcov, hC⟩ := iInf_lt_iff.mp hC
      obtain ⟨hCdiam, hCsum⟩ := iInf_lt_iff.mp hC
      have hCsum' : ∑' i, ediam (C i) ^ m < ENNReal.ofReal ε := by
        refine lt_of_le_of_lt (le_of_eq ?_) hCsum
        refine tsum_congr fun i => ?_
        rcases (C i).eq_empty_or_nonempty with he | hne

          rw [iSup_neg this, he, ediam_empty, zero_pow (by omega)]
          rfl
        · rw [iSup_pos hne, ENNReal.rpow_natCast]

      have hCeq : ∀ i, ediam (C i) = ENNReal.ofReal (D i) := fun i =>
        (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal (hCfin i)).symm
      have hD0 : ∀ i, 0 ≤ D i := fun i => ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
      have hDδ : ∀ i, D i ≤ δ / 2 := fun i =>
        ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal (by positivity) (hCdiam i)

subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (A : Set (Eucl P)), MeasurableSet A → CountablyRectifiable m A → ∃ (G : ℕ → Eucl m → Eucl P) (B : ℕ → Set (Eucl m)), (∀ p, ∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzWith K (G p)) ∧ (∀ p, MeasurableSet (B p)) ∧ (∀ p, InjOn (G p) (B p)) ∧ (∀ p, ∀ b ∈ B p, DifferentiableAt ℝ (G p) b) ∧ (∀ p, G p '' B p ⊆ A) ∧ (∀ p, MeasurableSet (G p '' B p)) ∧ Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint fun p => G p '' B p) ∧ (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) (A \ ⋃ p, G p '' B p) = 0

Library inputs (pinned Mathlib 25730c7c, SimonGMT 2b36630):
- (L2) Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02 (AreaLipschitz.lean): areaRegularSet f := {x | DifferentiableAt ℝ f x ∧ Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ f x)}.
  - measurableSet_areaRegularSet: this set is Borel.
  - area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero: if LipschitzWith K f, then for every s, μHE[finrank ℝ E] (f '' (s ∖ areaRegularSet f)) = 0. This is Rademacher plus the null critical image.
- (L4) exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/Jacobian.lean:255).
  - Input: f, s, f′ with HasFDerivWithinAt f (f′ x) s x for x ∈ s, and r : (E →L[ℝ] F) → ℝ≥0 with r A ≠ 0 for all A.
  - Output: pairwise disjoint Borel t_n with s ⊆ ⋃_n t_n, and A_n with ApproximatesLinearOn f (A_n) (s ∩ t_n) (r(A_n)), i.e. ‖f x − f y − A_n(x − y)‖ ≤ r(A_n)‖x − y‖ on s ∩ t_n.
  - Moreover, if s is nonempty then ∀ n, ∃ y ∈ s, A_n = f′ y.
- (L5) MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Polish/Basic.lean:821): a Borel set in a Polish space has Borel image under a map that is continuous and injective on it.
- (L6) LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith: an injective linear map L on a finite-dimensional space admits K > 0 with ‖v‖ ≤ K‖L v‖.
- Also used: finrank_euclideanSpace_fin (finrank ℝ (Eucl m) = m), and disjointed, disjoint_disjointed, disjointed_subset, iUnion_disjointed, MeasurableSet.disjointed.

1. (Data.) Unfold CountablyRectifiable m A. There are M₀ ⊆ E := Eucl P with μHE[m](M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : Eucl m → E (j ∈ ℕ) with LipschitzWith K_j F_j, such that A ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j.

2. (Lower-bound constants.) For every continuous linear L : Eucl m →L[ℝ] E choose δ(L) ∈ ℝ≥0 with δ(L) > 0, and κ(L) > 0:
- If L is injective, (L6) gives K_L > 0 with ‖v‖ ≤ K_L‖L v‖ for all v. Put δ(L) := κ(L) := (2K_L)⁻¹.
- Otherwise put δ(L) := κ(L) := 1.
Claim: let L be injective, t ⊆ Eucl m and g : Eucl m → E, and suppose ‖g(b) − g(b′) − L(b − b′)‖ ≤ δ(L)‖b − b′‖ for b, b′ ∈ t. Then κ(L)‖b − b′‖ ≤ ‖g(b) − g(b′)‖ for b, b′ ∈ t. Indeed,
  ‖b − b′‖/K_L ≤ ‖L(b − b′)‖ ≤ ‖g(b) − g(b′)‖ + ‖g(b) − g(b′) − L(b − b′)‖ ≤ ‖g(b) − g(b′)‖ + (2K_L)⁻¹‖b − b′‖,
so ‖g(b) − g(b′)‖ ≥ (2K_L)⁻¹‖b − b′‖.

3. (Partition of the regular set.) Fix j and put R_j := areaRegularSet F_j, which is Borel by (L2).
- If R_j = ∅, put t_{j,l} := ∅ for all l.
- Otherwise, F_j is differentiable at each b ∈ R_j, so HasFDerivWithinAt F_j (fderiv ℝ F_j b) R_j b. Apply (L4) with f := F_j, s := R_j, f′ := fderiv ℝ F_j and r := δ; this is allowed since δ(L) ≠ 0 for all L. It gives Borel sets t′_l and continuous linear maps A_l (l ∈ ℕ) with:
  - R_j ⊆ ⋃_l t′_l;
  - ApproximatesLinearOn F_j A_l (R_j ∩ t′_l) δ(A_l);
  - since R_j ≠ ∅, A_l = fderiv ℝ F_j y_l for some y_l ∈ R_j.
  Put t_{j,l} := R_j ∩ t′_l.
- In both cases: t_{j,l} is Borel, t_{j,l} ⊆ R_j, and R_j ⊆ ⋃_l t_{j,l}.
- F_j is injective on t_{j,l}. In the nonempty case, A_l is injective because y_l ∈ R_j. Step 2 then gives κ(A_l)‖b − b′‖ ≤ ‖F_j b − F_j b′‖ on t_{j,l}, so F_j b = F_j b′ forces ‖b − b′‖ ≤ 0, i.e. b = b′.

4. (Enumeration.) For p ∈ ℕ with (j, l) := Nat.unpair p, put G_p := F_j and S_p := t_{j,l}. Then:
- G_p is LipschitzWith K_j, hence continuous;
- S_p is Borel, and G_p is injective on S_p;
- G_p is differentiable at every b ∈ S_p, because S_p ⊆ R_j;
- G_p '' S_p is Borel by (L5), since Eucl m is Polish and G_p is continuous and injective on S_p.

5. (The exceptional set.) Put N := M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j '' (univ ∖ R_j). By (L2) with s := univ and finrank ℝ (Eucl m) = m, μHE[m](F_j '' (univ ∖ R_j)) = 0 for every j. Together with μHE[m](M₀) = 0 and countable subadditivity, μHE[m](N) = 0.

6. (Covering.) We show A ⊆ N ∪ ⋃_p G_p '' S_p. Let x ∈ A.
- If x ∈ M₀, then x ∈ N.
- Otherwise x = F_j(b) for some j and b.
  - If b ∉ R_j, then x ∈ F_j '' (univ ∖ R_j) ⊆ N.
  - If b ∈ R_j, then b ∈ t_{j,l} for some l. With p := Nat.pair j l we have Nat.unpair p = (j, l), so x = G_p(b) ∈ G_p '' S_p.

7. (Disjointification.) Let A_p := disjointed (fun p => A ∩ G_p '' S_p) p, i.e. A_p = (A ∩ G_p '' S_p) ∖ ⋃_{q<p} (A ∩ G_q '' S_q), and B_p := S_p ∩ G_p⁻¹(A_p).
(i) A_p is Borel (MeasurableSet.disjointed; A and every G_q '' S_q are Borel), A_p ⊆ A ∩ G_p '' S_p (disjointed_subset), and the A_p are pairwise disjoint (disjoint_disjointed).
(ii) B_p is Borel, since S_p is Borel, G_p is continuous (hence measurable) and A_p is Borel. Also B_p ⊆ S_p, so G_p is injective on B_p and differentiable at each point of B_p.
(iii) G_p '' B_p = A_p. If b ∈ B_p then G_p(b) ∈ A_p by definition. Conversely, if x ∈ A_p then x ∈ G_p '' S_p, so x = G_p(b) with b ∈ S_p; then b ∈ G_p⁻¹(A_p), i.e. b ∈ B_p.
Consequently each G_p '' B_p = A_p is a Borel subset of A, and the sets G_p '' B_p are pairwise disjoint.

8. (Null remainder.) ⋃_p A_p = ⋃_p (A ∩ G_p '' S_p) by iUnion_disjointed. If x ∈ A ∖ ⋃_p A_p, then x ∉ G_p '' S_p for every p; otherwise x ∈ A ∩ G_p '' S_p ⊆ ⋃_p A_p. So x ∈ N by Step 6. Hence A ∖ ⋃_p G_p '' B_p ⊆ N, and μHE[m](A ∖ ⋃_p G_p '' B_p) = 0.

9. The family (G_p, B_p)_{p∈ℕ} has all the required properties. ∎

- Since G is differentiable at b = tl(w), HasFDerivAt G L (tl w).
- tl is its own derivative, so the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp) shows that v ↦ G(tl v) has derivative L ∘L tl at w.
- pr₀ is its own derivative, so v ↦ (pr₀ v, G(tl v)) has derivative pr₀.prod (L ∘L tl) at w (HasFDerivAt.prodMk).
- Composing with the continuous linear map Λ gives HasFDerivAt G̃ (Λ ∘L pr₀.prod (L ∘L tl)) w.
- Hence fderiv ℝ G̃ w = L̃ := Λ ∘L (pr₀.prod (L ∘L tl)), i.e. L̃(v) = Λ(v_0, L(tl v)).

3. (Inner products.) For s, s′ ∈ ℝ and x, x′ ∈ Eucl P,
  ⟨Λ(s,x), Λ(s′,x′)⟩ = s·s′ + ⟨x, x′⟩.
Proof: write the EuclideanSpace inner product as a sum over Fin (P+1) (EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct) and split off the 0-th term (Fin.sum_univ_succ).

4. (Basis vectors.) Let E_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ Eucl (m+1) and e′_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1 ∈ Eucl m. Then:
- pr₀(E_0) = 1 and tl(E_0) = 0;
- for j : Fin m, pr₀(E_{j.succ}) = 0 because j.succ ≠ 0;
- for j : Fin m, tl(E_{j.succ}) = e′_j: coordinate k of tl(E_{j.succ}) is (E_{j.succ})_{k.succ}, which is 1 if k = j and 0 otherwise, since Fin.succ is injective.

5. (Gram matrix.) Let Γ̃_{ij} := ⟨L̃E_i, L̃E_j⟩ (i, j : Fin (m+1)) and Γ_{ij} := ⟨Le′_i, Le′_j⟩ (i, j : Fin m). By Steps 2–3,
  Γ̃_{ij} = pr₀(E_i)·pr₀(E_j) + ⟨L(tl E_i), L(tl E_j)⟩.
By Step 4 this gives:
- Γ̃_{00} = 1·1 + ⟨L0, L0⟩ = 1;
- Γ̃_{0, k.succ} = 1·0 + ⟨L0, Le′_k⟩ = 0;
- Γ̃_{i.succ, j.succ} = 0·0 + ⟨Le′_i, Le′_j⟩ = Γ_{ij}.

6. (Determinant.) Laplace expansion along row 0 (Matrix.det_succ_row_zero) gives
  det Γ̃ = Σ_{j : Fin (m+1)} (−1)^j·Γ̃_{0j}·det(Γ̃.submatrix Fin.succ j.succAbove).
- Split off j = 0 (Fin.sum_univ_succ). Every term with j = k.succ vanishes, because Γ̃_{0,k.succ} = 0.
- The j = 0 term is (−1)^0·1·det(Γ̃.submatrix Fin.succ (Fin.succAbove 0)) = det(Γ̃.submatrix Fin.succ Fin.succ), by Fin.succAbove_zero.
- By Step 5, Γ̃.submatrix Fin.succ Fin.succ = Γ entrywise. Hence det Γ̃ = det Γ.
- For m = 0 the same computation gives det Γ̃ = Γ̃_{00}·det(empty matrix) = 1 = det Γ.

This is exactly the claimed identity, since its left side is det Γ̃ and its right side is det Γ, with fderiv ℝ G̃ w = L̃ (Step 2). ∎

subproblem.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, K ∈ ℝ≥0, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^P with LipschitzWith K G, and B ⊆ ℝ^m Borel such that G is injective on B and differentiable at every point of B. Write Φ(s, x) := (s, x_1, …, x_P) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))) and π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))), with H^k := μHE[k]. Then for every Borel g : ℝ^{P+1} → [0, ∞]:
(1) φ(s) := ∫⁻_{G(B)} g(Φ(s, x)) dH^m(x) is a measurable function of s ∈ ℝ;
(2) ∫⁻_{{y : π(y) ∈ G(B)}} g dH^{m+1} = ∫⁻_ℝ φ(s) ds.
This is the product formula H^{m+1}⌞(ℝ × G(B)) = L¹ ⊗ H^m⌞G(B) for one injective Lipschitz piece.
